diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We say that $\omega$ or $X$ are $k$-homogeneous (or homogeneous of degree $k$) if:

    h_z^*\omega = z^k \omega

and respectively

    (h_z)_*X = z^kX$.

We say that $(P, \pi, h)$ is a \emph{homogeneous Poisson manifold} if $\pi$ is $-1$-homogeneous, i.e.
\[
(h_z)_* \pi = \frac{1}{z} \pi \quad \text{for all } z \in \mathbb{R}^\times.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed identity (h_z)_*Π = (1/z)Π is a wrong computation. Pushing forward Π = (1/t)Λ + ∂/∂t∧E by h_z(x,t)=(x,zt) gives (h_z)_*Π = zΠ (the 1/t factor contributes z after substituting t=t'/z and the ∂/∂t wedge contributes z from Th_z(∂/∂t)=z∂/∂t). Under the paper's convention (h_z)_*X = z^k X, this means Π is 1-homogeneous, not (−1)-homogeneous. The definition of homogeneous Poisson manifold demands (−1)-homogeneity, so the Poissonization does not satisfy it as stated. The root is a sign inconsistency: the multivector-field homogeneity convention should read (h_z)_*X = z^{−k}X (or the Poisson degree should be +1), and the proof computation must read (h_z)_*Π = zΠ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the definition of k-homogeneous multivector field to (h_z)_*X = z^{-k}X (or equivalently change the homogeneous-Poisson degree from −1 to +1) and correct the displayed computation in the proof from (h_z)_*Π = (1/z)Π to (h_z)_*Π = zΠ.
issues.overall_effect: The central claim that Poissonization yields a homogeneous Poisson manifold is false under the paper's stated definitions. The degree label used in the definition of hPHI and throughout the homogeneity bookkeeping is inconsistent, though the underlying geometric constructions (0-homogeneous sprays, 1-homogeneous symplectic forms) are verified independently and remain correct.
issues.title: Wrong homogeneity computation and sign inconsistency in Prop added-1
issues.why_classification: Two local sign corrections in a definition and a one-line proof computation restore full consistency; every substantive claim, construction, and downstream result survives with the corrected degree labels.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We call variation functions to any time-dependent functions $(f_s)_{s\in I}$ such that $df_s = \xi_s$, for all $s\in I$.

issues.failure_explanation: Variation functions are defined as any functions satisfying df_s = ξ_s, hence are determined only up to an additive constant. If ξ_s is 1-homogeneous then h_z^*f_s − z f_s is a constant c(z); adding a nonzero constant to f_s generally destroys 1-homogeneity (e.g., f_s + 1 is not 1-homogeneous even when f_s is). The implicit argument from the definition only yields: ξ_s is 1-homogeneous if and only if f_s can be chosen to be 1-homogeneous — strictly weaker than the claimed 'if and only if f_s are 1-homogeneous' for arbitrary variation functions.

failure_location.quote: Then $\xi_s$ are $1$-homogeneous if and only if $f_s$ are $1$-homogeneous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'if and only if f_s are 1-homogeneous' with 'if and only if f_s can be chosen 1-homogeneous' (equivalently add the normalization that f_s vanish at a reference point of each connected component of L_s).
issues.overall_effect: The corollary as stated is false in the 'only if' direction. Downstream uses that require 1-homogeneous variation functions (to obtain 1-homogeneous modified Hamiltonians for hPHI) must explicitly normalize f_s, otherwise the homogeneity of the modified Hamiltonian is not guaranteed.
issues.title: Corollary added-1 'only if' direction is false without normalization
issues.why_classification: A one-phrase qualification or additive-constant normalization repairs the statement and preserves every downstream claim and guarantee with no new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: when $L \xhookrightarrow{} (\Sigma,\omega)$ is a Lagrangian bisection for $R$, the induced map $\varphi_L = \beta\circ \alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ defines a Poisson diffeomorphism $(P,\Pi)\rightarrow (P,\Pi)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity φ^s_H = α∘φ^s_{α^*H}∘σ is false for the bi-realizations constructed in the paper. For the Weinstein realization (α = τ), α∘φ^s_{α^*H}∘σ = id ≠ φ^s_H. For the Karasev realization used in the example, α∘φ^s_{α^*H}∘σ(q,p) = (q−s/2, p) while φ^s_H(q,p) = (q+s, p). The correct relation is φ^s_H = β∘(α|_{L_s})^{-1} = φ_{L_s} (item 3, which is correct). The underlying theory (Coste-Dazord-Weinstein) factors the Hamiltonian flow through the target map β, not the source map α.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula in item 2 with φ^s_H = β∘(α|_{L_s})^{-1} (equivalently state item 2 in terms of φ_{L_s}, matching item 3), or delete item 2 and note that item 3 is the operative relation.
issues.overall_effect: The formula in item 2 is a false identity. However item 3 (φ^s_H = φ_{L_s}) is correct and is the result actually used in the construction of integrators, so no downstream formal result is invalidated. The homogeneity check in Section 6 verifies the wrong formula.
issues.title: Theorem ham flow item 2 states a false flow-factorization formula
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one formula in a cited theorem preserves every substantive claim and guarantee; the construction relies on item 3, which is correct.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: when $L \xhookrightarrow{} (\Sigma,\omega)$ is a Lagrangian bisection for $R$, the induced map $\varphi_L = \beta\circ \alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ defines a Poisson diffeomorphism $(P,\Pi)\rightarrow (P,\Pi)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims Theorem ham flow guarantees that for any Lagrangian bisection L the induced map φ_L is a Hamiltonian flow. The theorem only guarantees (item 1) that φ_L is a Poisson diffeomorphism, and (item 3) that φ_{L_s} equals a Hamiltonian flow for the specific family L_s = φ^s_{α^*H}(σ(P)). For a general Lagrangian bisection, φ_L is a Poisson diffeomorphism but not necessarily the flow of any Hamiltonian. The difference is that a Poisson diffeomorphism need not lie in the image of the sharp map Π^\sharp.

failure_location.quote: Theorem \ref{thm: ham flow} guarantees that, given a Lagrangian bisection $L$, the induced diffeomorphism $\varphi_L$ is a Hamiltonian flow.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to 'Poisson diffeomorphism' for general bisections and state that for bisections arising from the flow of α^*H (or, more generally, from an exact smooth family with 1-homogeneous variation functions) the induced maps form a Hamiltonian flow — the latter justified by the variation-function / Hamilton-Jacobi machinery of Section 5.
issues.overall_effect: The sentence misrepresents the theorem's scope and is then used to argue that the family (φ_{L_s})_s is a Hamiltonian flow (needed for the hPHI definition). The overclaim makes the subsequent hPHI construction claim unsupported unless a separate argument via the Hamilton-Jacobi theory of Section 5 is supplied.
issues.title: Overclaim that Theorem ham flow guarantees φ_L is a Hamiltonian flow
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening to the scope actually covered by the theorem (or a short reference to the Section 5 Hamilton-Jacobi argument for the specific family used in the construction) preserves the main construction and all downstream guarantees; no new lemma or construction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: constructing a suitable approximation of the variation functions $(\mathcal{H}_s)_s$ that coincides with $ H^P$ of order $k$

issues.failure_explanation: The claim asserts that the family (φ_{L_s})_s satisfies the hPHI definition of order k. This requires (i) that (φ_{L_s})_s is the exact flow of a time-dependent homogeneous Hamiltonian (𝓗_s)_s and (ii) that 𝓗_s = H^P + o(s^{k-1}). Neither is proved. The paper says 'constructing a suitable approximation of the variation functions' but does not carry out the construction, does not show that the variation functions of (L_s)_s determine a Hamiltonian on P whose flow is (φ_{L_s})_s, and does not verify the order-of-accuracy condition linking the approximation quality of the variation functions to the modified equation. These are nontrivial steps connecting the Lagrangian-bisection variation theory of Section 5 to the modified-equation framework of the hPHI definition.

failure_location.quote: the induced family of diffeomorphisms $(\varphi_{L_s})_{s\in I}$ is a homogeneous Hamiltonian Poisson integrator of order $k$ for $H^P$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the missing argument: (i) show that for an exact smooth family of homogeneous Lagrangian bisections with 1-homogeneous variation functions f_s the induced maps (φ_{L_s})_s constitute the exact flow of the time-dependent homogeneous Hamiltonian 𝓗_s obtained from f_s via the source map α|_{L_s}; (ii) prove the order estimate 𝓗_s = H^P + o(s^{k-1}) from the stated approximation quality of the variation functions. The tools for step (i) are partially present in Section 5 (Prop added-3, Cor added-1, the Hamilton-Jacobi analysis) but the connecting argument is not given; step (ii) requires a perturbation estimate not present in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's main advertised deliverable — the existence and construction of homogeneous Poisson Hamilton Integrators of order k and, via Poissonization, Jacobi Hamiltonian Integrators of order k — is not established. Only the structure-preservation property (Poisson diffeomorphism, same symplectic leaf) is supported by the cited results; the order guarantee and the modified-Hamiltonian characterization are unsupported.
issues.title: Claim that construction yields hPHI of order k is unsupported
issues.why_classification: Completing the proof requires a contained nontrivial argument (linking variation functions to modified Hamiltonians on P and a perturbation estimate for the order) that goes beyond routine algebra but avoids new global proof architecture; the Section 5 tools provide the ingredients. The main construction and its rate guarantee survive once the argument is supplied.
